description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 The Community You Will Join: 
 The Community Support org handles tens of millions of interactions yearly, engaging with Airbnb customers by phone, messaging, chat, or social media channels. The group handles hundreds of issues across categories including Cancellations, Account Issues, Refunds, Payments, Reservations, Extenuating Circumstances, Booking & Listing issues, Safety & Claims. The organization is globally distributed with offices in San Francisco, Dublin, Montreal, Seattle, Singapore, Manila, Gurgaon and an extensive partner network serving all regions. 
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 We are looking for a seasoned Forecasting and Demand Planning Analyst on our Community Support (CS) team. This individual is responsible for demand forecasting and long-term planning across multi-channel contact center operations for our Global Operations team. This role ensures the organization has the right resources, at the right time, with the right skills to meet service level objectives while optimizing cost and productivity.
 The role combines planning, advanced analytics and business partnership to drive scalable, data-driven workforce decisions in a complex, fast-changing environment.
 A Typical Day:  
 Demand Forecasting & Statistical Modeling
- Own short-term, mid-term, and long-term demand forecasting across all Global Operations teams and channels (phone, messaging, email, back-office etc.).
- Design, develop, and maintain statistically robust demand forecasting models using time series and machine learning techniques (e.g., exponential smoothing, ARIMA, regression-based models etc.).
- Perform trend, seasonality, and variance decomposition; detect structural breaks, outliers, and demand anomalies.
- Quantify forecast uncertainty through confidence intervals, error distributions, and bias analysis.
- Perform scenario modeling for peak demand periods, product launches, growth initiatives, and unplanned demand events.
- Continuously assess model performance using statistical accuracy metrics (MAPE, RMSE, MAE, bias etc).
- Establish model governance standards, including documentation, validation, back-testing, and post-mortem analysis.
- Research, prototype, and implement new forecasting and optimization techniques as business needs evolve.
- Perform scenario planning and sensitivity analysis to quantify trade-offs between service levels, cost, and utilization.
 Advanced Analytics
- In partnership with the Analytics and Data Engineering team, design and build scalable planning data pipelines, dashboards, and automate forecasting and capacity models to improve scalability, repeatability, and timeliness.
- Use SQL and Python to extract, transform, and analyze large-scale operational datasets to monitor forecast accuracy, capacity gaps, utilization, and operational risk.
 Decision Support & Stakeholder Communication
- Present forecast assumptions, methodologies, risks, trade-offs, and recommendations in clear, executive-ready formats and act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and participate in demand/capacity planning discussions in cross-functional forums.
- Align cross-functional stakeholders (Delivery, Product, Finance, HR, and others) to embed planning outputs into execution and operational decision-making.
- Identify and implement process improvements, automation, and best practices in the demand and capacity planning area to optimize cost while maintaining or improving customer experience and service-level outcomes.
 Your Expertise: 
- 10+ years of experience in demand forecasting, capacity planning, workforce analytics, or applied analytics.
- Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Operations Research, Engineering, Economics, Data Science, or a related quantitative field.
- Strong foundation in probability, statistics, and optimization.
- Hands-on experience building and validating forecasting models (time series analysis, exponential smoothing, ARIMA, regression, hypothesis testing) and capacity models (Erlang, queueing theory, service-level and utilization modeling).
- Strong understanding of contact center metrics (AHT, ASA, service level, shrinkage, occupancy); experience supporting large-scale, multi-site, or global contact center environments preferred.
- Advanced analytical skills with strong proficiency in Excel, Google Sheets, SQL, Python and data visualization tools such as Tableau.
- Experience with WFM tools (e.g., NICE, Verint, Aspect) or planning platforms (e.g., Anaplan) preferred.
- Strong business acumen with the ability to balance cost efficiency and customer experience outcomes.

We have a huge responsibility to our community of Hosts and guests to be there when things don’t go exactly as planned with their reservations. We have a lot of work to do in the coming years and we are looking for someone who will help us manage all of the things that need to be done to deliver best-in-class services to our community.    
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 As a Complex Claims Manager in the Complex Claims,  you will play a vital role in safeguarding the integrity of our Aircover platform by effectively identifying, investigating, and managing  the risk and mitigation strategies in resolution of Complex and Large Loss claims.
 You'll manage partners to influence prioritization, drive accountability, deliver improvements, and scale changes on claims which impact Airbnb. You'll work with internal and external partners to influence prioritization, drive accountability, and deliver improvements.  
 You will work closely with cross-functional teams to manage emerging risks / threats while enabling business growth in various markets. Philosophy will be to identify intelligence / risk gaps and work with other internal risk management teams (such as Trust team, and Safety team), third party adjusters, our partners, Platform Product Management, Global Crisis Management, Community support, Policy, Privacy Legal teams to strengthen Airbnb’s platform.
 You will be reporting at Monthly, Quarterly and Annual Business Reviews for your area. You will serve as a thought leader with stakeholders such as Trust, Legal, Privacy, Safety, Product Management, Policy, and understand how the policy/product roadmap impacts risk mitigation of emerging threats. 
 A Typical Day:  
- Management, Policy, and understanding how the policy/product roadmap impacts risk and exposure mitigation. 
- Builds partnerships and is responsible for engaging in the Large Loss Claim reviews with our insurers on a monthly / quarterly basis depending upon the insurer/market.  Ensure we are managing insurers claim handling and potential coverage/relationship issues as well as material reserve changes that could impact Airbnb and the Captive. 
- Craft a Resolution Plan for Complex and Large Loss Claims driving the Carrier and/or TPA to resolve the claim while meeting the needs of internal stakeholders.
- Partner with Legal, GCM, Trust and our Brokers, Insurers, Outside Counsel, and TPA’s on complex claims resolution which may also involve coverage issues and settlement authority.
- Accountable for performance and results Insurance Carrier and Partners worldwide over Complex Claims which may impact policy limits or trigger need of notice to Brokers and Carriers under the insuring policies.
- Mentorship of L6 and L7 Host Damage Protection and Host Liability Protection Specialist on claims.  Works to upskill L6 and L7 partners for growth and development.  Supports the team by guiding through complex claims and changes. 
- Management of claims which impact Airbnb Financials and the Captive.
- Work closely with cross-functional teams to manage the Risk and Exposure on Complex and Large Loss Claims. 
- Collaborate with internal departments, such as other Aircover Ops teams, legal, Trust, CS safety to share claim  insights, improve claim handling by our Carriers and TPA’s while developing a Resolution Plan to bring a claim to the correct conclusion.
- Ensure compliance with company policies, procedures, and legal requirements related to claims handling
- Mentor to others by simplifying complex information which includes claims knowledge, data analysis, business information, and process obstacles.

- Proven ability to communicate clearly and effectively to audiences of varying technical levels.

description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 La communauté qui vous attend : 
 Le directeur ou la directrice principal·e de la qualité des niveaux de volume, est le ou la seul·e responsable de la mesure de la qualité, des données et de l'amélioration continue pour toutes les fonctions de soutien à la communauté d'Airbnb de plus grand volume. Ce rôle est responsable du programme de qualité de bout en bout pour : 
- Anglais mondial (GE)
- Reste du monde (ROW, qui comprend 9 langues différentes)
- Soutien supérieur
 Les programmes Anglais mondial et Reste du monde couvrent plusieurs niveaux de service : résolutions 1, 2 et 3, Soutien au service dédié (DSS), Soutien géré dédié aux hôtes (DMHS), et ils sont soutenus par un réseau mondial de partenaires opérant en tout temps dans des dizaines de langues.
 Votre contribution : 
 Il s'agit d'un poste de direction de haut niveau qui se situe au croisement de la stratégie et de l'exécution. Le directeur ou la directrice principal·e de la qualité éliminera le cloisonnement au sein de l'organisation de la qualité, établira un modèle opérationnel unifié et utilisera des outils basés sur l'IA pour développer les données sur la qualité. Il ou elle travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de prestation de services, de formation, d'amélioration des processus opérationnels et d'autres parties prenantes pour assurer l'alignement sur les priorités, régler les problèmes et veiller à ce qu'Airbnb fournisse à son réseau mondial de partenaires un ensemble unifié de priorités. 
 Le candidat ou la candidate retenu·e s'imposera comme un partenaire crédible auprès des parties prenantes et jouera un rôle de porte-parole de la qualité pour le portefeuille des niveaux de volume à l'interne.
 Journée type :  
 Leadership stratégique et responsabilité du programme 
- Prendre en charge et exécuter la stratégie de qualité pour les niveaux de volume en fonction de plusieurs priorités essentielles : éliminer le cloisonnement, s'aligner avec les parties prenantes, définir un modèle opérationnel clair et générer un impact mesurable.
- Consolider les cadres d'assurance qualité fragmentés des programmes Anglais mondial et Reste du monde en un modèle opérationnel unifié, en éliminant les processus incohérents, les approches divergentes pour les mauvais indices de recommandation client et les signaux de qualité incompatibles.
- Présenter la qualité des niveaux de volume pendant les réunions sur les rapports d'activités hebdomadaires, mensuelles et trimestrielles, et dans les forums de planification interfonctionnels, en plus d'apporter une perspective proactive et narrative qui donne de la visibilité à la direction avant que des problèmes ne soient signalés pendant des examens opérationnels.
 Mesure et exécution de la qualité 
- Superviser l'exécution de l'évaluation de l'assurance qualité sur tous les sites partenaires des niveaux de volume dans le monde entier en assurant l'application cohérente des processus et des cadres d'assurance qualité.
- Mener des analyses des causes profondes des défaillances systémiques, en traduisant les conclusions issues de l'assurance qualité en recommandations relatives aux produits, aux processus et aux politiques qui vont au-delà de l'accompagnement des agents.
- Formaliser l'audit de l'auditeur en tant que contrôle continu : définir la sélection des échantillons, les seuils d'alignement, l'analyse des causes profondes et les processus de correction au niveau des évaluateurs.
- Veiller à ce que chaque évaluation se termine par une mesure d'accompagnement formalisée et mettre en place des mécanismes de suivi permettant de déterminer si cet accompagnement se traduit par une amélioration du rendement au fil du temps.
 Observations, rapports et partenariat avec les parties prenantes 
- Établir des rapports d'indicateurs clés de performance automatisés pour tous les sites, tous les niveaux et toutes les langues des niveaux de volume en éliminant les processus manuels. 
- Unifier l'analyse des mauvais indices de recommandation client dans l'ensemble des programmes Anglais mondial et Reste du monde pour mettre en évidence en temps réel des tendances globales.
- Élaborer une fiche d'évaluation du rendement des partenaires en matière d'assurance qualité en définissant clairement les responsabilités relatives à la précision de l'étalonnage, à l'exhaustivité de l'évaluation, à la détection des erreurs critiques et à l'efficacité de l'accompagnement.
 IA et mise en œuvre technologique

On a l'énorme responsabilité envers notre communauté d'hôtes et de voyageurs d'être présents quand leurs réservations ne se déroulent pas exactement comme prévu. On a beaucoup de travail à accomplir dans les prochaines années et on cherche une personne qui nous aidera à gérer tout ce qui doit être fait pour offrir des services exceptionnels à notre communauté.
 Votre contribution : 
 En tant que gestionnaire des réclamations complexes, vous jouerez un rôle essentiel dans la protection de l'intégrité de notre plateforme Aircover en déterminant, en étudiant et en gérant efficacement les stratégies de risque et d'atténuation pour résoudre les réclamations de pertes complexes et importantes.
 Vous gérerez les partenaires pour définir les priorités, renforcer la responsabilité, apporter des améliorations et faire évoluer les réclamations qui affectent Airbnb. Vous travaillerez avec des partenaires internes et externes pour définir les priorités, renforcer la responsabilité et apporter des améliorations.  
 Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec des équipes transversales pour gérer les risques émergents tout en permettant la croissance de l'entreprise sur divers marchés. La philosophie sera d'identifier les lacunes en matière d'intelligence et de risque et de travailler avec d'autres équipes de gestion des risques internes (comme l'équipe Confiance et l'équipe Sécurité), des experts tiers, nos partenaires, la gestion des produits de la plateforme, la gestion des crises mondiales, le soutien à la communauté, les politiques et les équipes juridiques de la confidentialité pour renforcer la plateforme Airbnb.
 Vous ferez des rapports lors des examens mensuels, trimestriels et annuels des activités commerciales de votre région. Vous agirez en tant que visionnaire avec des parties prenantes (p. ex. : confiance, juridique, confidentialité, sécurité, gestion des produits, politiques), et comprendrez l'incidence des politiques et de la feuille de route des produits sur l'atténuation des risques liés aux menaces émergentes. 
 Journée type :  
- Gérer, orienter et comprendre l'incidence des politiques et de la feuille de route des produits sur l'atténuation des risques et de l'exposition. 
- Être responsable de l'examen des réclamations pour pertes importantes avec nos assureurs sur une base mensuelle ou trimestrielle, en fonction de l'assureur ou du marché.  Vous assurer qu'on gère les attentes des assureurs et qu'on garde une longueur d'avance sur tout problème potentiel de couverture ou relationnel ainsi que sur les changements matériels importants qui pourraient affecter nos prévisions. 
- Gérer les réclamations qui affectent Airbnb Financials et la compagnie d'assurance captive.
- Élaborer un plan de résolution des réclamations pour pertes complexes et importantes qui incite l'assureur ou l'administrateur tiers à résoudre la réclamation tout en répondant aux besoins des parties prenantes internes.
- Coordonner les réclamations de pertes complexes et importantes avec les services juridiques, GCM, et de confiance, ainsi que nos courtiers, assureurs et administrateurs tiers sur des cas complexes qui peuvent aussi impliquer des problèmes de couverture ou d'autorisation. 
- Être responsable du rendement et des résultats des compagnies d'assurance et des partenaires dans plusieurs emplacements dans le monde sur les réclamations complexes qui peuvent avoir une incidence sur les limites de la police ou nécessiter d'aviser les courtiers et les compagnies d'assurance en vertu des polices d'assurance.
- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes transversales pour gérer les risques et l'exposition dans des réclamations de pertes complexes et importantes. 
- Collaborer avec les services internes tels que les autres équipes d'Aircover Ops, les services juridiques, la confiance et la sécurité du SC pour partager les informations sur les réclamations et améliorer leur traitement par nos assureurs et les administrateurs tiers tout en élaborant un plan de résolution pour mener une réclamation à la conclusion souhaité

- Work cross-functionally with Strategic Finance, Data and Analytical Engineering,and Data Science teams to ensure alignment and leverage synergies.

Reporting to the Head of Payment Partnerships, this role is pivotal in managing the partnerships that ensure our hosts are paid reliably, efficiently, compliantly and in alignment with our growth and platform goals.
 You will lead business development, deal negotiation, and strategic relationship management for a portfolio of high-value payment partners. With a focus on impact and long-term alignment, you'll help craft our partner landscape, structure and renegotiate commercial agreements, and serve as a critical voice in expanding and optimizing how payments to hosts are enabled around the world.
 A Typical Day:  
 Strategic Partner Leadership
- Define and evolve our payout partner strategy in collaboration with the broader Payments, Product, Compliance and Finance teams to ensure coverage, performance, and alignment with Airbnb’s strategic and financial goals.
- Identify the right partners in each market, structure new deals, and renegotiate existing relationships to optimize for cost, reliability, reach, and innovation.
- Drive global deal execution for payouts—developing commercial structures, navigating regional regulatory constraints, and shaping contracts to meet Airbnb’s evolving needs.
 Relationship Management & Performance
- Own and cultivate high-impact relationships with financial institutions, payment processors, banks, and other key partners, managing executive-level engagement to ensure Airbnb is a priority client.
- Monitor partner performance rigorously, identify gaps or opportunities, and lead cross-functional efforts to address issues or evolve terms.
- Lead strategic business reviews and act as the point of escalation and problem resolution for performance or operational misalignment.
 Global Payments Strategy & Influence
- Assist in the ongoing scaling of Airbnb’s payout infrastructure—ensuring that partner decisions reflect regional needs, market conditions, cost structures, and regulatory environments.
- Partner cross-functionally with Legal, Treasury, Risk, Product, Engineering, and Global Operations to align execution with global strategy.
- Stay ahead of industry and macroeconomic changes affecting international payments and proactively bring forward opportunities and risk mitigation strategies.

- Demonstrated success in owning commercial negotiations and managing multi-million dollar partnerships that balance customer experience, innovation, and financial return.
- Proven ability to craft and execute partner strategies that result in measurable business growth and process improvement.

- Experience working with regulators or regulated partners in cross-border payout env

 The Principal, Strategic Finance & Analytics, Incubations role will partner closely with business, product, and analytics leaders across Luxe, Monthly Stays, and Airbnb for Business. This role will directly support the investment decisions behind Airbnb's fastest growing emerging businesses.
 We sit at the intersection of finance, strategy, and the business, partnering directly with leaders to decide where Airbnb invests, how we grow, and what we do next. We expect every member of the team to bring a CFO mindset to budget management, producing actionable insights, owning our performance story, and supporting day-to-day execution.
 Why join us: 
- A seat at the table. We're advisors, not just analysts. Our work shapes real decisions, not just decks.
- A steep learning curve. Small, lean teams and a focus on internal mobility means broad exposure across product and business areas.
 If you like ambiguity, moving fast, and building the answer instead of just reporting it, you'll fit right in.
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 As a Principal in Strategic Finance & Analytics supporting Luxe, Monthly Stays, and Airbnb for Business, you will be highly visible and partner with senior leaders across each business to accelerate their path to scale. You will become the subject matter expert on the economics of these businesses, including how demand and supply are acquired, what they cost, and what they return. You will bring a strong point of view on where we should be investing more, where we should be investing differently, and what we need to prove before we invest at all.
 This role requires a strong commercial mindset, with the ability to size opportunities, evaluate returns, and translate performance and funnel insight into clear business implications and strategic recommendations for senior leadership. Because these are incubation businesses, the analytical foundation often does not yet exist, so you will build it. The ideal candidate relishes the opportunity to roll up their sleeves, and is a self-starter comfortable embracing the adventure of a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.
 A Typical Day:  
- Investment Decision Support: Build the business cases behind major investment decisions across Luxe, Monthly Stays, and Airbnb for Business. Size the opportunity, model the returns, and frame the tradeoffs so leadership can decide where to place bets and how large those bets should be
- Performance Management: Own end to end performance management for the incubation portfolio, including forecasting, goal and OKR setting, and executive reporting. Build scalable reporting frameworks that connect early signals to revenue and long term value
- Full Funnel Analytics: Track and analyze full funnel performance across demand and supply for each business. Identify where the funnel leaks, why, and what it is worth to fix
- Unit Economics and Scalability: Establish and pressure test the unit economics of each business. Determine which parts of the model improve with scale, which do not, and what needs to be true for these businesses to become material contributors
- Capital Allocation Across the Portfolio: Assess how investment is allocated across the incubation businesses relative to their potential. Recommend reallocation where returns and readiness diverge from where capital is going today
- Presentations to Leadership: Synthesize complex data into clear narratives and recommendations for senior leadership. Influence cross functional stakeholders to drive alignment on high impact investment and operating decisions

- Advanced SQL proficiency with the ability to independently extract, analyze, and synthesize data
- Superb financial modeling skills and extensive experience conducting quantitative and qualitative financial analysis
- Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate data into decisions
- Excellent communication skills, with experience presenting to senior leadership
- Proven ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment
- High ownership mindset with strong judgment and attention to detail
- Experience evaluating growth strategies, ROI/efficiency returns, and the scalability of new business models is a big plus

Groceries waiting when you land, a ride from the airport, your bags stored between checkout and your flight, a car to explore beyond city limits. - Balance both sides of the marketplace. Partner with the supply and operations teams building the provider side, so that what's great for guests is also sustainable for the hosts and partners delivering the service. 
- Drive clarity across orgs. Bring engineering, design, marketing, ops, legal, and leadership along with a clear strategy.

- Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills across business, partnerships, engineering, design, and data science.

description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 The Community You Will Join:  
 Fraud & Safety Delivery (FSD) is at the heart of keeping Airbnb safe for the millions of hosts and guests who trust our platform every day. As part of Global Operations, FSD reviews and resolves potential fraud and safety cases across the full user lifecycle, with internal and partner specialists operating 24/7 across the globe.
 You'll sit in Frontline Operations, working alongside the operations managers who run our frontline teams, including the vendor teams who deliver alongside us. Your closest partners are Advanced Analytics, Capacity Planning, Quality Analytics, Business Intelligence and Tools Support.
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 Right now, when a frontline metric moves, it takes several teams and several days to work out why, and the answer often arrives after the moment to act on it has passed. This role changes that. You will be the single accountable answer on specialist-driven performance for Frontline Operations: what moved, which specialists, queues, vendors or sites it came from, and what we should do about it.
 Success looks like root causes and recommendations delivered in hours rather than days, and a growing share of performance issues you surfaced resolved before they hit a top-line metric.
 A Typical Day:  
- Break down frontline performance by specialist, queue, vendor and site — analysing operational data to get to the level of detail the question actually needs.
- Root-cause specialist-driven moves in SLA, AHT, accuracy and utilisation, and deliver one accountable answer rather than a set of possibilities. For example: tracing an ATOQ SLA drop to a specific staffing change on a specific site, with the size of the effect quantified.
- Monitor specialist-level metrics for problems that never show up in the top-line numbers, and take a recommendation — not just a finding — to Frontline Delivery leadership.
- Write the requirements for specialist metrics and dashboards, and refine them with Tools Support, so the reporting frontline managers use every day answers their real questions.
- Work the boundaries deliberately: hand causes that aren't specialist-driven to Business Intelligence, take Capacity Planning's approved volume forecasts as an input, and use Quality Analytics' case audits as evidence.
- Sit in weekly business reviews and operational escalations, explaining what the data means to people who need to make a decision in the next ten minutes.
- Use AI tooling as a first resort rather than a last one, including our internal AI data analytics tools, to get to an answer in minutes instead of hours.
 Your Expertise: 
- 8+ years in operations analytics, workforce analytics, business intelligence or a comparable analytical role, in an environment where operational decisions were made on your numbers.
- You write your own SQL to a high standard — complex joins, window functions, and the judgement to know when a result is wrong. You will not be building dashboards; you'll be specifying them.
- Deep contact-centre or high-volume operations knowledge: you understand SLA, AHT, occupancy, shrinkage, adherence and how a staffing decision on one site shows up in a queue metric two weeks later.
- Proven root-cause work in a multi-vendor, multi-site delivery model, where the answer sits somewhere between staffing, skilling, tooling and process — and you're able to say which.
- You give one clear answer and stand behind it. You're comfortable saying what the data cannot tell us, and equally comfortable explaining to a senior leader that their assumption is wrong.
- Clear, direct communicator — you can take a complex analysis and give a frontline manager the one sentence they need to act on.
- Experience in Trust, Fraud, Safety or another high-stakes operations environment is a plus, not a requirement — the instincts for urgency and precision matter more.

Since then, Airbnb - and now Airbnb.org - has helped provide safe housing for over 250,000 people to date in response to hundreds of emergency events around the world including hurricanes, wildfires, refugee crises, and a global pandemic. The Airbnb.org team within Airbnb works in support of the Airbnb.org non-profit and partners with Hosts, nonprofit organizations, emergency management agencies and governments to provide stays to people around the world in times of crisis, and has announced a series of commitments to diversity, equity and inclusion including centering marginalized communities in its work and in team composition.

 Airbnb.org operates like a small startup inside Airbnb. Our data team is lean, the problems are new, and there is no established playbook for most of what we do. That means your ingenuity and autonomy are welcome and  you will have the room to decide what to build and how, to experiment, and to shape the way a growing, mission-driven organization uses data. 
 Analytics Engineers build the data foundation for the whole team - which translates to impact on all stakeholders with insights, analysis and experimentation. As a Senior Analytics Engineer, you will own major projects that build out the data foundation for Airbnb.org: designing and delivering the data models, metrics and dashboards that power our reporting, analysis and experimentation, and continuously raising the bar on data quality and reliability for the systems you build. Many of these projects will start out vaguely defined, and you will bring structure to them by breaking down the work, weighing tradeoffs, and delivering solutions that are efficient, reliable and simple to maintain. You will bring strong expertise in metric development, dimensional data modeling, SQL, Python, and distributed data processing frameworks, and a solid understanding of how the pieces of a modern data stack fit together.

You will partner closely with stakeholders across Marketing, Fundraising, Programs, Product and Engineering to understand their data needs, translate business questions into well-defined metrics and data products, and prioritize your work in line with Airbnb.org's goals. You will work alongside our existing data team - Analytics Engineer, Analyst and Data Scientist - sharing knowledge, seeking and giving feedback, and collaborating with Data Engineering and Data Platform teams to get things built.

- Design, define and implement metrics and dimensions for Airbnb.org, and document them clearly so they are trusted and used consistently across teams
- Own data quality for the tables and pipelines you build: implement testing, auditing and validation, respond to data incidents, and follow through on corrective actions that go beyond the immediate fix
- Identify and improve or deprecate low-quality or duplicative data assets, and plan quality improvements into the team's roadmap

We build specialized models for mission-critical trust and safety problems, develop the AI agents and agentic capabilities that automate trust decisions, and create the benchmarks and evaluation harnesses that keep decision quality high as those agents take on more autonomy. We work on problems before the answer is known — prototyping, experimenting, and iterating with our partner teams until a solution proves itself against real business and top line metrics.

You'll own and deliver ML projects end-to-end, from framing an ambiguous problem and prototyping a solution, to training and productionizing models, to proving impact on top line metrics with front line teams.
 You'll work on abuse behavior detection that spans multiple defenses, on AI agents that make trust decisions autonomously, and on the evaluation and benchmarking work that makes those decisions trustworthy.  At Airbnb, we maintain and extend a world-class payments platform that is the engine of commerce and trust for our global community. This platform currently supports 220 countries and over 65 currencies, connecting dozens of payment providers and processing billions of dollars annually. To enable and support growth of the marketplace, we continually innovate unique ways for guests to pay for stays and experiences that are memorable and in many cases life changing.  Whether it's providing accepting relevant forms of payments, breaking payments into more manageable parts, or combining payments for several individuals seeking to travel and share together, Airbnb strives to make paying trips as simple as possible, while protecting our guests and hosts with security and assurances we have their backs every step of the way. 
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 Within the payment organization, the platform team comprises individuals that manage our products and experiences related to checkout, payment methods, risk, compliance, and hosts payouts.  We are seeking a strong Senior Platform leader to manage all aspects of our guest payment capabilities and experiences.  This includes enabling new global and local payment methods, onboarding and validating methods with our processing partners, managing post transaction interactions such as refunds and transaction reporting, and finally creating and expanding our growing portfolio of installments and financing solutions to help pay for trips and trip related services.  This role is a key leadership position within the platform product organization and will report into our Global Director of Payments Platform Product management. 
 A Typical Day:  
- Deliver and evolve Guest Payments Platform Strategy & Roadmap: Lead the development and execution of the Payments platform strategy and roadmap for Guest Pay-ins, refunds, payment plans, methods and processing resilience.  This also includes product leadership working alongside engineering on redundancy,vaulting, processor performance and optimization and availability across the entire payment funnel.
- Manage Execution & Delivery: Oversee the end-to-end product development lifecycle for the various sub domains within the guest payment team, from concept and feasibility analysis to execution, launch, and post-launch optimization.
- Lead Cross-Functional Teams: Guide and collaborate with cross-functional teams (Engineering, Design, Product Marketing, Platform Risk, Compliance, etc.) to deliver high-quality capabilities and ensure dependencies are managed effectively.
- Team Leadership & Development: Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of senior platform managers, fostering a culture of excellence and innovation.
- Contribute to overarching Payment Platform Strategy: Act as a key contributor to the broader payments platform strategy, providing expert insights on the competitive landscape, emerging technologies, and consumer trends.
- Stakeholder Management & Communication: Manage stakeholder expectations and present plans, progress, and outcomes to senior leadership and other cross-functional partners to ensure alignment and influence outcomes.
- Operational Excellence: Define and monitor key product metrics, ensuring product quality and continuous improvement to meet operational and business goals.

- 12+ years of product management experience in inbound (pay-ins) and outbound (pay-outs) money movement within a payments, finance, or heavily transactional company.
- Proven product management experience with a deep understanding of stakeholder needs.
- Strong interpersonal skills: able to push back, ask questions, and challenge others while creating lasting, collaborative partnerships.
- Experience working directly with non-product teams such as legal, tax, compliance, risk, and payments operations.
- Direct experience working with Engineers.
- Startup experience: comfortable with a fast pace, changing needs, and limited resources. Bonus points if you have also worked at large, scaled organizations and can balance the best of both worlds.
- Ability to synthesize large amounts of unstructured and diverse information into a single, clear set of requirements.
- Global perspective: experience building products for different countries and cultures.
- Bonus points for experience with global and local payment methods that are not credit cards and experience across Payments, Risk, and Compliance systems and tools.

- Rest of World (ROW; which is comprised of 9 different languages)

 This is a senior leadership role operating at the intersection of strategy and execution. The Senior Quality Lead will break down silos within the Quality organization, establish a unified operating model, and leverage AI-powered tools to scale quality insights. This leader will work closely with Service Delivery, Training, Business Process Improvement, and other stakeholders to ensure alignment on priorities, remediate issues, and ensure Airbnb is providing its global partner network a unified set of priorities. 
 The successful candidate will establish themselves as a credible partner to stakeholders and be recognized internally as the voice of quality for the Volume Tier portfolio.

 Strategic Leadership & Program Ownership 
- Own and execute the Volume Tier quality strategy aligned to several critical priorities: breaking silos, aligning with stakeholders, defining a clear operating model, and driving measurable impact.
- Consolidate fragmented QA frameworks across GE and ROW into a unified operating model, eliminating inconsistent processes, divergent NPS detractor approaches, and incompatible quality signals.
- Represent Volume Tier quality in WBRs, MBRs, QBRs, and cross-functional planning forums; bring a proactive, narrative-led perspective that gives leadership visibility before problems surface in operational reviews.
 Measurement & Quality Execution 
- Oversee QA evaluation execution across all Volume Tier partner sites globally, ensuring consistent application of QA processes and frameworks.
- Lead root cause analysis on systemic failures, translating QA findings into product, process, and policy recommendations that go beyond agent-level coaching.

- Ensure every evaluation closes with a documented coaching action; build the tracking mechanisms to measure whether coaching is translating into performance improvement over time.

- Establish automated KPI reporting across all Volume Tier sites, tiers, and languages, eliminating manual processes. 
- Unify NPS detractor analysis across GE and ROW, ensuring global patterns surface in real time.
- Build a Partner QA Performance Scorecard, establishing clear accountability for Calibration Accuracy, Evaluation Completeness, Critical Error Detection, Coaching Effectiveness.

- Lead the deployment of AutoQA (via Observe.AI) across Volume Tiers; partner with the Platform team to ensure appropriate sequencing.
- Build and govern a clear accountability framework for AI-assisted quality tools and processes.

- Foster a One-Quality-Team culture that eliminates the cross-team divides: shared best practices, cross-regional learning, and proactive knowledge sharing.
- Set high expectations and hold the team accountable for output quality, insight delivery, and stakeholder engagement.
- Partner closely with peers to ensure one consistent quality voice across the portfolio.

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 The Community you will join: 
 Our Supply Enablement & Activation Team is growing and we want you to be part of it! Airbnb is looking for a seasoned Senior Manager, Supply Enablement to join our team. In this role, you'll lead a team of enablement and activation specialists responsible for building world-class content, training programs, and GTM activation at scale — equipping our field, vendor, and operations teams with the knowledge, skills, and tools to consistently acquire, grow, and retain high-quality supply across Homes, Hotels, Services, and Experiences.
 The difference you will make: 
 This role requires candidates to be based in the US. This role is not eligible for relocation support. 
 This is a high-impact leadership role for someone who has lived the reality of frontline sales and account management, knows how to build and develop high-performing enablement teams, and has a sophisticated command of AI-powered tools to make enablement smarter, faster, and more measurable. You'll set the strategic direction, raise the bar on quality and craft, and ensure everything your team produces drives real, measurable behavior change in the field.
 A typical day:  
- Team Leadership & Development 
- Lead, coach, and develop a team of enablement managers and activation specialists responsible for content creation and curation, training development, and GTM program delivery; Set clear goals, priorities, and quality standards across the team
- Build team capacity and capabilities, including identifying skill gaps, investing in development, and hiring exceptional talent
- Enablement Content & Program Strategy
- Co-own with Enablement Director and Foundations + Quality Enablement Manager, the end-to-end enablement content strategy — ensuring your team focused on ‘front of house’ produces high-quality, audience-specific, evergreen assets including playbooks, pitch decks, objection handling guides, onboarding curricula, and certification programs. Guide your team in leveraging AI for content development, personalized learning, coaching at scale, and practice — pushing the boundaries of what's possible with the tools in your stack
- Translate CBO and Supply strategy into actionable enablement plays, working closely with your team to bring them to life for field, vendor, and scaled ops audiences and developing strong working relationships with those teams
- Set and uphold a high bar for enablement deliverables from onboarding to upskilling — ensuring content doesn't just inform, but changes behavior and drives measurable performance outcomes.
- GTM Activation
- Partner deeply with regional leads (EMEA, AMER, APAC) and cross-functional stakeholders to land new product launches, strategic initiatives, policy & legal approved positioning, and sales plays in the field effectively and on time
- Build a strong feedback loop between the field – across all 4 lines of business – and your team, so activation is continuously informed by what's actually working on the ground
- Cross-Functional Partnership & Measurement
- Work closely with RevOps, Product, Marketing, Community, and Policy to embed enablement insights into strategic initiatives and keep field teams ready to execute
- Regularly report program performance, ROI, and team impact to senior leadership with clarity and credibility; Partner with Advanced Analytics to design experiments (A/B, ERF) that prove the incrementality of your team's investments
 Your expertise:  
- 12+ years of experience in sales enablement, revenue enablement, or a closely related field — ideally within a high-growth tech or marketplace company
- 3+ years managing and developing enablement or GTM teams — you know how to hire great people, set a high bar, and bring out the best in a team

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 The Community You Will Join: 
 Airbnb’s mission is to create a world where people can Belong Anywhere. As we work to achieve that mission, our cross functional Tech Operations and Programs team helps enable Tech organizations to execute and deliver on high impact programs and initiatives. 
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 You will decide what the engineering world knows about Airbnb.
- Our engineers solve hard problems at scale across infrastructure, data, and applied AI — and they write about that work well. Almost none of the engineers we'd most like to hire have ever seen it.
- You'll change that, and the change is measurable. A year in, senior candidates should arrive already able to describe our technical work accurately, because they found it before we found them. Our engineers should be recognised names in their fields rather than anonymous authors. Airbnb should be the source people cite on at least one technical domain. And the strongest engineers in the market should have a reason to choose us that has nothing to do with the offer.
- That is a rare kind of impact for this discipline. Most tech brand roles are asked to manufacture credibility that isn't there. Here the engineering is genuinely strong and already documented — the gap is that it doesn't travel. You'd be building the function that closes it, with real autonomy, very little inherited process, and direct access to engineering leaders and our CTO.
 A Typical Day: 
- Own the editorial engine. Run the Airbnb Tech Blog end to end: sourcing topics from teams, coaching engineer-authors, editing to a high bar, and moving posts through legal, security and comms review without letting them stall. Set and hold a publishing rhythm the org can rely on.
- Find the cross-team narratives. Our biggest gap is that individually strong posts never add up to a story. You'll work across orgs to identify the themes that connect work from multiple teams, and publish them as connected sets — while each domain keeps publishing in depth for its own specialists.
- Build our voices. Help our engineers and technical leaders develop genuine public presence: bylines, talks, speaker coaching, and a pipeline of new voices. This includes partnering closely with our CTO to establish his public technical presence.
- Own distribution. Establish our canonical home on an Airbnb-owned domain, stand up the surfaces we're missing including video, and decide what our social channels are for. Publishing well and distributing poorly is the pattern we're here to break.
- Run our external presence. Set conference and event strategy — where we speak, where we sponsor, where we skip — and manage what we host ourselves. Own our academic collaborations and technical media relationships, and the budget and vendors behind all of it.
- Steward our open source presence. Make sure what Airbnb claims publicly is accurate and actually maintained, and that the projects carrying our name reflect how we want to be seen.
- Prove it works. Partner with Talent Acquisition to connect this work to hiring outcomes — inbound share of the senior pipeline, offer acceptance at staff level and above in ML and infrastructure — and be honest about what is and isn't attributable.
 Your Expertise: 
- Substantial experience in technical content, developer relations, engineering communications or technical editorial — including time spent working directly with engineers, not adjacent to them.
- Technical fluency. You don't need to write production code, but you need to hold your own in a systems design conversation, read a design doc, and judge whether a draft post says anything real. Credibility with staff engineers is the difference between this role working and not working.
- Editorial judgment and hands-on craft. You can edit an engineer's draft into something sharper without flattening their voice, and you know the difference between a post that teaches something and one that announces something.
- Influence without authority. Nothing you need is owned by you. You've built systems and incentives that got busy senior people to produce, rather than relying on persistence.
- Program discipline. You've owned events, budgets and vendors end to end, and you're comfortable with the unglamorous half of the job.
- Measurement literacy. You connect brand work to funnel outcomes, and you're straight about the limits of attribution rather than reaching for impressions.
- Judgment on risk. You've navigated legal and security review, and you know what shouldn't be published as well as what should.

Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 The Community You Will Join: 
 Airbnb’s Business Technology (Biztech) organization sits at the heart of how we scale our internal operations to match the pace and ambition of our products. Within Biztech, the Finance Accounting Platform team owns the core finance accounting platform — the system that records, processes, and reports the financial lifecycle of every product Airbnb offers to the world.
 As a Senior Platform Manager on this team, you will be embedded in a rich, cross-functional community spanning the full breadth of Airbnb’s business. You’ll partner daily with Product and Platform Managers across Payments, Trust, Guest & Host, Pricing, Insurance, Hotels, and Customer Service — as well as Finance stakeholders from Revenue Controllership, Treasury, Tax, Payments Legal, Consolidation, Collections, and Cash. You’ll work closely with Data Engineers and Oracle Applications teams to bring platform solutions to life, and collaborate with FP&A and Business Unit teams who depend on the data your platform produces.
 This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance, product, and engineering — and who finds energy in being the connective tissue across a large, diverse, and highly capable community.
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 You will be the strategic and operational owner of the finance accounting platform — the single point of accountability for shaping how it evolves to support Airbnb’s growing portfolio of product offerings.
 Your impact will be felt across three dimensions:
 Scaling the platform with Airbnb’s ambitions — You will define and drive the long-term roadmap for the finance accounting platform, ensuring it can scale to support new product lines, geographies, and business models. You will own prioritization across a high-volume platform funnel — balancing competing requests with clarity and structured decision-making — and continuously identify opportunities to optimize platform performance and reliability.
 Bringing new products to life on the accounting platform — Every time Airbnb launches or evolves a product, there is an accounting story that needs to be told accurately and at scale. You will lead that effort end-to-end — from initial accounting impact assessment through solution design, engineering alignment, UAT, release coordination, and production normalization — translating complex product changes into well-designed accounting workflows that record product lifecycle financials to Oracle FAH GL.
 Strengthening the financial foundation — You will help define and refine data pipeline monitoring controls, support month-end close processes, and partner with Finance stakeholders to automate manual operational workflows. Your work will directly improve the accuracy, timeliness, and reliability of financial data that flows across Airbnb’s Finance organization and beyond.
 A Typical Day:  
 No two days look the same, but here’s a window into what you might be doing:
- Syncing with a cross-functional Product Manager from the Payments or Hotels team to understand an upcoming product change and assess its downstream accounting implications
- Reviewing a technical spec with Data Engineering to align on the implementation approach for a new accounting workflow feeding Oracle FAH
- Running a UAT session with Revenue Controllership and Tax stakeholders to validate that a new product’s financial lifecycle is being recorded accurately before it goes to production
- Pulling and analyzing ad hoc data using SQL to support a Finance or FP&A team working through a close question or business case
- Triaging and prioritizing new requests coming into the platform funnel — aligning stakeholders on sequencing and tradeoffs against the broader roadmap
- Reviewing data pipeline monitoring alerts and working with engineering to resolve a control gap before it impacts month-end close
- Leading a working session with Treasury or Collections to map out an opportunity to automate a high-touch manual process
- Drafting a platform update for a senior Finance stakeholder that translates a complex technical change into clear business impact
 Your Expertise: 
 Accounting & Finance Domain 
- Subject matter expert in accounting principles and ASC 606 revenue recognition, with the ability to apply standards to complex, multi-product digital marketplace environments
- Proven experience implementing end-to-end accounting workflows across quote-to-cash cycles, including reporting and reconciliation
- Hands-on experience supporting B2C product workflows on finance platforms — ideally at a high-growth, high-transaction-volume technology company

Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 The Community You Will Join:  
 Our hosts are opening their homes or providing experiences to guests from around the world. We’re creating new relationships & placing people in vulnerable situations. Therefore trust is the fundamental currency of Airbnb. We are the Trust & Safety team, composed of engineers, data scientists, designers, product managers, and operations, responsible for earning this trust by building for safety at each moment of the guest and host journey. We build cutting edge machine learning models to detect risk, defenses to deter risky actors, and operations tools that enable investigators worldwide. We define community standards and policies, set high expectations, and keep bad actors out while providing delightful experiences for good users. 
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 As a Product Manager in the Trust & Safety team, you will identify customer pain points, business opportunities, and define/deliver the products that help us create a safe and trusted community around the world. Your work will be pivotal to shaping the future of hospitality and travel. Within the Trust & Safety team, you’ll be focused on Safety: To reduce safety incidents (e.g. interpersonal harm and illegal activities). 
 A Typical Day:  
- Creating vision and strategy for Trust & Safety products and platforms. 
- Leading a cross-functional working group of engineers, data scientists, designers, operations experts, and policy experts to ensure alignment, execution, and launches
- Maintaining product backlog and the product roadmap. Own prioritization process of product solutions based on business value and customer impact
- Defining goals and success with clearly measurable objectives and key results. 
- Building alignment across product teams (inside and outside of Trust & Safety), and Leadership/Executive teams.
- Anticipating bottlenecks, making tradeoffs and balancing the business needs, customer needs, versus technical or operational constraints.
- Presenting product roadmap and status to the business and Airbnb leadership on an ongoing basis. Communicate concisely and influence outcomes.
- Evaluating new product opportunities and bring forward proposals (buy, build, partner solutions) for new capabilities with data and users at the forefront 
- Developing short term plans aligned with long term goals to iteratively build platform capabilities to defend against safety issues
- Becoming the thought leader and entrepreneur that others within Airbnb look up to for knowledge, processes, and methods on building products and platforms
 Your Expertise: 
- 5+ years product management experience
- Prior product, operation, or engineering experience in trust, safety, risk or fraud 
- Outstanding written and verbal communication ability to a diverse stakeholder audience, including a global team of C-level executives, product, and technical stakeholders
- Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills
- Experience building machine learning products or technical product management
- Experienced in design, and hypothesis driven product development
- Entrepreneurial drive to achieve stretch goals in an innovative fast-paced environment
- Exceptional collaboration, partnership and influencing skills with the ability to work in a global environment across multiple locations and time zones to drive consensus across teams
- Experience leading teams through ambiguity, and high stakes trade off decisions

 The Lead Program Manager, Workplace Operations is responsible for leading and scaling programs that span the Workplace Operations organization. This role operates across functions and geographies, owning programs end-to-end while building the structure, processes, and tools that enable the broader team to operate consistently and at scale. 
 Currently, the Workplace Operations team is made up of multiple teams delivering at a high bar across a global office footprint, each with its own processes, tools, vendors, and rhythms. This role exists to look across all of it: to understand how the work actually gets done today, find where effort is duplicated or handoffs break down, and design a more connected and automated way of operating. It is equal parts program delivery and operational modernization.

 This is a cross-functional role that requires strong program management fundamentals, independent judgment, and the ability to influence stakeholders without direct authority. You will build a clear picture of how Workplace Ops teams work today, surface the gaps and opportunities that get in the way of efficiency and alignment, and turn that into a strategic and scalable roadmap: what we should build in-house, what is better delivered through vendors, and most importantly what can be automated with AI. 
 The ideal candidate is comfortable working in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, skilled at building clarity and alignment, curious about how emerging technology changes operational work, and motivated by improving how teams operate and deliver for employees globally. 
 A typical day: 
- Own and manage a portfolio of cross-functional programs with global scope, driving delivery from inception through ongoing operation and continuous improvement 
- Develop and maintain program-level policies, processes, playbooks, and operating standards that enable the Workplace Ops team to deliver consistently across regions and functions 
- Lead cross-functional workstreams in partnership with teams across the organization, ensuring Workplace Ops priorities are clearly represented, aligned, and delivered 
- Identify gaps in current program offerings and proactively develop solutions, often without an established playbook 
- Build and scale operational tooling, workflows, and internal resources that improve team effectiveness and the consistency of the employee-facing experience 
- Develop measurement frameworks and synthesize data and feedback to assess program performance, identify improvement opportunities, and inform strategic decisions 
- Support the team’s internal operating model by contributing to goal-setting, roadmap development, and team ways of working 
- Manage vendor relationships and provide direction where relevant to program delivery, ensuring alignment to Airbnb standards 
- Serve as a thought partner to Workplace Ops leadership on organizational priorities, team capacity, and program strategy 
- Communicate effectively across all levels of the organization, translating complex operational topics into clear guidance and actionable recommendations

- Map how Workplace Ops teams operate today — processes, tools, systems, vendors, and handoffs — and build a shared, evidence-based view of the current state across functions and regions 
- Identify gaps, duplication, manual effort, and friction points where teams could run more efficiently, and size the opportunity so investment decisions are grounded in data 
- Create alignment and synergy across teams that operate independently today, consolidating overlapping workflows and standardizing where standardization helps, while preserving local flexibility where it matters 
- Develop clear build / buy / automate recommendations: what capability we should build in house, what is better delivered through vendors and managed service partners, and what should be automated 
- Lead the identification and adoption of AI-enabled workflows — from intake, triage, and routing to reporting, knowledge management, and employee self-service — and turn promising ideas into scoped, measurable pilots 
- Partner with IT, Technology, Procurement, Finance, Legal, Privacy, and Security to evaluate tools and platforms, define requirements, and ensure new solutions meet Airbnb standards for data handling, security, and responsible AI use

 The Community You Will Join: 
 Guest & Host Technology builds the end-to-end experience that connects people around the world. Our team owns the identity and privacy layer beneath that experience: the systems that determine who can see what about whom, in what context, and why. That includes migrating how the rest of the company references users (moving from raw, global user identifiers to relationship-scoped identity), and building the privacy controls behind features like trip sharing and profile visibility. Get this layer wrong and it either breaks trust or breaks the product; our job is to make sure it does neither. 
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build and scale the backend systems behind user identity and privacy. You'll be reasoning about relationship-scoped access (who's allowed to see this, given the specific context they're asking from), and building systems that other teams across the company depend on to do the same correctly.
 You'll work across true backend fundamentals: service architecture, data modeling, authorization logic, and migration tooling that needs to run safely at Airbnb's scale without breaking the dozens of teams who consume these systems.
 A Typical Day:  
- Design and build backend services and APIs that enforce identity and privacy rules consistently across the company's product surfaces
- Contribute to large-scale migrations (e.g., moving service and client code off legacy identity patterns) — including the tooling that makes those migrations safe to run broadly, not just the one-off fixes
- Define and evolve authorization logic for context-scoped data access, and reason clearly about edge cases (e.g., who's allowed to see what, and why that answer differs by relationship or product surface)
- Partner with the teams building on top of your systems — messaging, trips, profile, and beyond — to make sure privacy primitives are usable and hard to misuse
- Participate in design and code reviews, and raise the bar for correctness on a part of the codebase where mistakes are costly
- Debug and resolve production issues with clear, structured root-cause analysis rather than surface-level fixes
 Your Expertise: 
- 6+ years of professional backend software engineering experience, with strong fundamentals in service-oriented architecture, API design, and data modeling
- Proficiency in Java and/or Kotlin, and comfort working within a microservices environment (RPC frameworks, service IDLs, dependency injection)
- Experience designing systems with correctness and authorization as first-class concerns, not an afterthought
- A track record of shipping migrations or infrastructure changes that other teams depend on, with attention to backward compatibility and rollout safety
- Strong written communication. You can clearly document a problem, its root cause, and trade-offs between solutions before escalating or proposing a fix
- Comfort with ambiguity: you can take a complex, evolving privacy or identity requirement and turn it into a concrete technical design without needing every detail spelled out

 The Difference You Will Make: 
 We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who can operate as a true dual-platform native engineer — someone with solid, current fluency in both iOS and Android. You'll own features end-to-end across both apps, and you'll be one of the people trusted to make architectural calls that need to hold up identically on Swift and Kotlin.
 You'll write production code on both platforms, and you'll also be expected to think beyond any single feature: flagging where our two native codebases are drifting apart, where a shared contract (like our GraphQL client layer) needs to evolve, and helping less experienced engineers ramp into dual-platform work.
 A Typical Day:  
- Design and ship features across our iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) native codebases, often the same initiative, shipped in parallel on both platforms
- Partner with design and product to translate one product spec into two platform-idiomatic implementations, rather than porting one platform's UI onto the other
- Uphold architecture, performance, and app-size standards that apply equally to both platforms
- Weigh in on shared client contracts (schema, logging, testing frameworks) consumed by both apps, and flag when a change would let the platforms drift apart
- Help other engineers ramp into dual-platform work through pairing and code review
- Participate in technical reviews and architecture discussions where your judgment is expected to span both platforms, not just one
 Your Expertise: 
- 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with deep, current, hands-on expertise in both native iOS (Swift, UIKit/SwiftUI) and native Android (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose), not legacy exposure to one platform and active work on the other
- A track record of independently shipping medium-to-large complexity features on either platform without ramp-up, and the ability to read, debug, and reason about the other platform's code even where you're less deep
- Solid opinions on mobile architecture, backed by experience keeping two independent native codebases coherent at scale
- Comfort owning a feature end-to-end with real ambiguity, and identifying when a decision needs to be escalated versus made independently
- Experience partnering closely with design and product to translate ambiguous requirements into concrete, platform-appropriate implementations

description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. 
 The Community You Will Join:
 At Airbnb, our mission is to create a world where anyone can belong anywhere. The Foundational Data team builds and operates the high-quality, widely reused datasets that power critical decisions across Airbnb: how visitors are measured from site traffic, how bot traffic is separated from organic traffic, and how cloud costs are attributed to Airbnb services. Our cost dashboards are among the most-used at Airbnb, relied on by technical leads, finance, and executives. Every dollar Airbnb spends running its infrastructure is attributed by models this team owns.
 We are now building a third pillar, and it puts this team at the forefront of how Airbnb measures AI: the cost, usage, and performance of the models we train and serve ourselves, and of the AI tools our own engineers use every day. When Airbnb asks whether an AI investment is paying off, the answer comes from datasets this team builds.
 Foundational Data sits inside Cloud Infrastructure and is a deliberate mix of Data Engineers and Analytics Engineers working as one team.
 The Difference You Will Make:
 As a Senior Staff Data Engineer, you are the technical leader for this team and the person who sets its direction. This is a hands-on role with no direct reports: you will own the long-term data architecture and you will build against it, from the Airflow-orchestrated pipelines that ingest telemetry, logs, and billing data through to the dimensional models and Minerva definitions that thousands of people at Airbnb reason with. Because we are a mixed DE and AE team, you will work across both disciplines: this role needs data engineering depth, plus enough fluency in metric and dimensional modeling to set direction for the analytics engineering side.
 Infrastructure intelligence is where you will start, and it is fresh ground. The signals describing our fleets are fragmented across cost, utilization telemetry, service performance, and GPU and model telemetry. Nobody has modeled this coherently yet, and the AI side is the least charted part of all. There is no schema to inherit. You would decide what these datasets are, then bring the rest of the company along.
 This work carries regular visibility to directors and VPs across Infrastructure and Finance.
 A Typical Day:
- Provide technical leadership across the team's data engineering and analytics engineering work, spanning cloud cost, traffic & bots, and infrastructure intelligence
- Define and own the multi-year data strategy and architecture for Airbnb's foundational data assets, and build the cross-org consensus needed to fund and execute it
- Own how Airbnb measures its AI: the unit economics of training and serving our own models, GPU fleet utilization, and the cost and adoption of developer AI tooling
- Design and build the datasets that integrate cost, utilization, performance, and reliability signals across Airbnb's infrastructure fleets, starting from a blank page
- Stay hands-on in the pipelines and models you architect, close enough to the build to catch the problems design reviews miss
- Influence and coach a distributed team of Data Engineers and Analytics Engineers, raising the quality bar through design and code review and scaling it by building the frameworks and automated checks other teams adopt
- Navigate conflicting stakeholder requirements across Infrastructure, Finance, Data Science, and Product Engineering, and land a single definition everyone can build on
- Identify and eliminate duplication and data fragmentation across the engineering organization, driving deprecation of what your models replace
- Participate in the team's on-call rotation for the datasets we own
 Your Expertise:
 You do not need prior experience with cloud cost, infrastructure, or AI/ML data to succeed here. What we cannot teach is the following.
- 12+ years of relevant industry experience with a BS/Masters, or 9+ years with a PhD, in data engineering or a closely related field
- You have designed, built, and operated production data pipelines at large scale, and you write strong SQL and Python. Scala experience is useful but not required
- You can design a dimensional model and define a metric others will trust, even if analytics engineering has not been your job title
- You have moved into an unfamiliar data or technical domain and become productive quickly, building enough understanding of the underlying systems to model them well
- You have been the technical lead on a team or program, setting direction that other senior engineers executed against without formal authority over them, while still writing code yourself

 Airbnb's Creative Studio is part of the team that establishes and maintains the voice — and the judgment — behind everything we write, generate, and publish at scale. You'll sit alongside writers and creative directors in a group that thinks about language the way a great designer thinks about visuals: with precision, taste, and an instinct for what's right versus what's merely correct. Your closest cross-functional partner will be Marketing Technology, whose teams build and tune the language models and editorial tooling you'll help shape. You'll also partner regularly with Legal, Trust, and Localization to ensure editorial standards and processes hold up across markets, languages, and regulatory considerations.

 You'll be responsible for shaping and maintaining Airbnb's brand voice and guidelines, training and refining the AI models that generate copy at scale, and serving as the final line of editorial judgment on AI-generated output before it reaches the world. This role is for someone whose taste and standards quietly define what "sounds like the brand" means, extended into an AI-assisted production pipeline. You won't just be proofreading — you'll be defining what "good" means for a system that writes at a scale no human team could match alone, and making sure it never loses the craft, warmth, and precision that language deserves.

- Review and refine AI-generated copy across campaigns, product, and marketing surfaces — catching not just errors, but tone, nuance, and craft issues an automated system would miss.
- Build and maintain scalable editorial QA processes for AI-generated content, defining what requires human review versus what can ship autonomously.

 The Community You Will Join: 
 The Quality & Blueprint team sits at the center of how Airbnb understands and improves the customer experience. We partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Finance to identify where the experience is breaking down, why it's breaking down, and what to do about it, so we can keep delighting the Airbnb community at scale. Our work informs strategy at the leadership level and decisions at the product squad level.
 The Difference You Will Make: 
 This role will act as a senior analytics leader on the Community Blueprint Quality team. You'll deliver high-impact analysis, experimentation, and reporting that drives how the business diagnoses and improves the guest and host experience. This is a hands-on, execution-focused role designed to accelerate progress during a period of constrained capacity. You will operate independently, partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders, and own end-to-end work from problem framing to leadership-ready recommendations.
 A Typical Day: 
- Conduct strategic deep dives into customer experience drivers (cleanliness, check-in, communication, etc.) to identify symptoms, diagnose root causes, and recommend interventions.
- Design, execute, and analyze experiments (A/B tests and quasi-experiments) to measure the impact of quality and blueprint initiatives.
- Build and apply causal inference frameworks (diff-in-diff, synthetic controls, propensity matching) to estimate the true impact of product, policy, and operational changes.
- Leverage LLMs and AI-assisted analytics to extract structured insights from unstructured data and to scale root-cause taxonomy generation across millions of trips.
- Develop and validate metrics and dimensions that monitor customer experience health and surface emerging quality issues.
- Build and maintain analytical artifacts (queries, dashboards, readouts) that let stakeholders self-serve on standard questions.
- Partner with Product, Engineering, Data Science, Data Engineering, and other Advanced Analytics teams to align on methodology, assumptions, and interpretation.
- Translate complex analyses into clear, concise insights and recommendations for senior leadership.
 Your Expertise: 
- 10+ years of experience in advanced analytics, data science, or applied quantitative analysis (industry experience required).
- Strong hands-on expertise in SQL and at least one programming language (Python or R).
- Proven experience designing and analyzing A/B experiments and applying statistical methods to real-world product problems.
- Experience with causal inference techniques (diff-in-diff, synthetic controls, propensity scoring) and a track record of applying them to ambiguous business problems.
- Hands-on experience with AI-assisted analytics workflows (Claude, ChatGPT, internal LLM agents) including prompt engineering, structured extraction from unstructured text, and using LLMs as classifiers or judges.
- Experience building metrics end-to-end, including definitions, validation, and implementation in data pipelines.
- Strong analytical judgment, ability to balance rigor with speed and clearly communicate tradeoffs.
- Excellent communication skills with experience presenting to senior, non-technical audiences.
- Demonstrated ability to operate independently, manage multiple priorities, and deliver against agreed timelines.
